::: {.callout-note title="Current project state"}
The multiscale coefficient-recovery pipeline, logarithmic sparsity model, barycentric temporal regularizer, analytical gradients, full-state continuation, automatic parameter-selection prototype, fixed-$X$ dictionary update, and controlled alternating coefficient/dictionary recovery have now been numerically validated.

The current dictionary-learning benchmark reproduces the 20 dB `gaussian_ramp_overlap_sine2` problem from the reference MATLAB workflow. The Python implementation includes the MATLAB-compatible flat initialization, exact 10-scale rational grid, L1-to-log sparse schedule, coefficient and dictionary over-relaxation, adaptive ADMM penalties, and padded Fourier-domain coefficient update.

A focused oracle-development sweep identifies $\lambda_S=0.24$ as a useful 20 dB reference. After a 100-iteration prefit and 200 additional non-temporal MCDL iterations, the learned Gaussian and ramp have cosine similarities $0.99243$ and $0.88441$, respectively, with 158 significant coefficients compared with 160 in truth.

The next phase is temporally regularized joint dictionary learning initialized from this validated non-temporal prefit. The value $\lambda_S=0.24$ is an oracle-development reference, not yet an unsupervised parameter-selection result.
:::

# Abstract

We develop a temporal regularization framework for nonnegative multiscale convolutional dictionary learning (MCDL) in which sparse coefficient representations evolve along finite-duration curves in joint shift--scale--time space. Each active frame should contain only one or a small number of significant coefficients, those coefficients should move smoothly through physical shift and scale coordinates, and a trajectory should be free to appear and disappear without being forced to persist throughout the observation interval.

The model combines a nonconvex logarithmic sparsity penalty with a barycentric temporal regularizer consisting of a trajectory-motion term and a gated within-frame spread term. A smooth squared activity gate satisfies both $g(0)=0$ and $g'(0)=0$, permitting natural track birth and death. All temporal components possess explicit gradients and require no inner transport optimization.

The optimization problem remains nonconvex. Numerical experiments show that full-state ADMM continuation is important for tracking favorable sparse branches. A hierarchical automatic parameter-selection procedure based on expected-noise discrepancy, stable parameter regions, and L-curve ideas is developed and evaluated against a post-hoc synthetic oracle.

The fixed-dictionary coefficient model has now been extended to joint dictionary learning. The fixed-$X$ dictionary operator, adjoint, normal equation, projection, and scale-normalization update have been independently validated. In addition, the principal non-temporal initialization workflow of the reference MATLAB Gaussian/ramp example has been reproduced in Python. At 20 dB, the resulting alternating MCDL estimator recovers a near-exact Gaussian atom, a recognizable ramp atom, and essentially the correct sparse support size. This establishes a controlled non-temporal learned-dictionary baseline for the next temporally regularized stage.

# Problem formulation

Let

$$
X(n,k,j,t)\ge0
$$

denote the coefficient tensor, where $n$ is shift, $k$ is dictionary-atom index, $j$ is scale, and $t$ is time. The data model is

$$
S=\mathcal A_DX+N.
$$ {#eq-forward}

For fixed dictionary $D$,

$$
\widehat X=\arg\min_{X\ge0}\left\{
\frac12\|\mathcal A_DX-S\|_F^2
+\lambda_SR_{\log}(X;a)
+\lambda_TR_T(X)
\right\}.
$$ {#eq-main}

The active temporal model is

$$
R_T(X)=R_{\mathrm{motion}}(X)+\beta_VR_{\mathrm{spread}}(X).
$$ {#eq-complete-temporal}

# Logarithmic sparsity regularization

The nonconvex logarithmic penalty is

$$
R_{\log}(X;a)=\frac1a\sum_i\log(1+aX_i),\qquad X_i\ge0.
$$ {#eq-logpen}

For the general coefficient-recovery solver, continuation evolves $a$ from $a_{\min}=10^{-4}$ toward $a_{\max}=0.95/\lambda_S$.

## MATLAB-compatible sparse schedule for dictionary initialization

The reference Gaussian/ramp MCDL initialization uses a related but distinct schedule. For iterations $r\le20$, it uses ordinary nonnegative $\ell_1$ shrinkage,

$$
Y=\left[X_r+U-\frac{\lambda_S}{\rho_X}\right]_+.
$$

Beginning with iteration 21, the update switches to logarithmic shrinkage with fixed

$$
a=\frac{0.95}{\lambda_S}.
$$

This compatibility schedule is used only in the Banco-style dictionary-learning reproduction. The previously validated stateful continuation formulation remains the active coefficient-recovery implementation for the general temporal estimator.

# Scaled dictionary atoms

Let $d_k\in\mathbb R^M$ be base atom $k$ and $M_j$ the rational resampling operator. Define

$$
\widetilde d_{k,j}=M_jd_k,
$$

and

$$
\alpha_{k,j}=\frac1{\|M_jd_k\|_2},\qquad
d_{k,j}=\alpha_{k,j}M_jd_k.
$$ {#eq-alpha}

During a dictionary update, $X$ and $\alpha$ are held fixed so that the forward map remains linear in the base dictionary.

# Barycentric temporal representation

For atom $k$ and frame $t$, define mass

$$
m_{k,t}=\sum_{n,j}X(n,k,j,t),
$$

and normalized frame distribution

$$
p_{n,j,k,t}=\frac{X(n,k,j,t)+\delta/(LJ)}{m_{k,t}+\delta},\qquad \delta=10^{-10}.
$$

The position and log-scale barycenters are

$$
\bar n_{k,t}=\sum_{n,j}p_{n,j,k,t}n,
\qquad
\bar\xi_{k,t}=\sum_{n,j}p_{n,j,k,t}\log s_j.
$$

The activity gate is

$$
g(m)=\frac{m^2}{m^2+\mu^2},\qquad
 g'(m)=\frac{2m\mu^2}{(m^2+\mu^2)^2},
$$

so $g(0)=g'(0)=0$.

The motion regularizer penalizes adjacent-frame barycenter displacement, while the within-frame spread term penalizes diffuse representations having similar first moments.

# Noise model and parameter selection

Noise is generated as

$$
N_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2),
$$

with

$$
\sigma^2=\frac{\|S_{\mathrm{clean}}\|_F^2}{N_{\mathrm{obs}}10^{\gamma/10}}.
$$

The expected-noise discrepancy is

$$
D_{\mathrm{exp}}=\frac12N_{\mathrm{obs}}\sigma^2,
$$

and

$$
r_D(\theta)=\frac{\frac12\|\mathcal A_DX-S\|_F^2}{D_{\mathrm{exp}}}.
$$

The established fixed-dictionary selector uses hierarchical $\lambda_S$, $\lambda_T$, and $\beta_V$ searches based on expected-noise discrepancy, tradeoff geometry, and solution stability. Synthetic truth is retained only for post-hoc oracle analysis.

# Fixed-dictionary Monte Carlo milestone

A development study used 10 independent realizations at each of

$$
\mathrm{SNR}\in\{20,17,14,11,8\}\ \mathrm{dB}.
$$

Under nested L-curve selection, exact position-scale trajectory recovery rates were

$$
[100,90,70,20,10]\%.
$$

The paired temporal-versus-nontemporal study showed that temporal regularization most consistently suppresses extraneous coefficients and stabilizes the intended compact trajectory representation. The searched temporal oracle also produced lower median coefficient error than the non-temporal oracle over most tested SNRs.

# Dictionary-learning extension

## Dictionary ADMM update

For fixed $X$ and $\alpha$, define

$$
(\mathcal B_{X,\alpha}D)_t=\sum_{k,j}(\alpha_{k,j}M_jd_k)*x_{k,j,t}.
$$

The dictionary subproblem is

$$
D^{(\ell+1)}=\arg\min_D\left\{
\frac12\|\mathcal B_{X,\alpha}D-S\|_F^2
+\frac{\rho_D}{2}\|D-G^{(\ell)}+H^{(\ell)}\|_F^2
\right\},
$$

with normal equation

$$
(\mathcal B_{X,\alpha}^*\mathcal B_{X,\alpha}+\rho_DI)D
=
\mathcal B_{X,\alpha}^*S+\rho_D(G-H).
$$

The projected update is

$$
G_k=\frac{[D_{r,k}+H_k]_+}{\|[D_{r,k}+H_k]_+\|_2},
$$

followed by recomputation of $\alpha$ and the scaled dual update.

## Dictionary validation results

The fixed-$X$, fixed-$\alpha$ dictionary forward operator was validated for linearity to relative error $2.81\times10^{-16}$ and for adjoint consistency to relative error $1.57\times10^{-14}$. The analytical dictionary objective gradient was validated by finite differences with best relative error approximately $1.08\times10^{-13}$.

The matrix-free dictionary CG solution agreed with an explicitly assembled direct solve to relative error $5.87\times10^{-13}$, with relative normal-equation residual $1.86\times10^{-12}$. The nonnegative unit-norm projection and scale-normalization update were separately validated.

Known-$X$ noiseless experiments recovered one and two dictionary atoms essentially exactly. For the two-atom experiment, the final learned-versus-true similarity matrix was approximately

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
1.000000 & 0.606691\\
0.606690 & 1.000000
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

# Reference Gaussian/ramp problem

The current alternating benchmark reproduces the synthetic `gaussian_ramp_overlap_sine2` configuration from the reference MATLAB workflow.

The dimensions are

$$
N=80,\qquad M=41,\qquad T=80,\qquad K=2,\qquad J=10.
$$

The rational scale set is

$$
\mathcal S=\left\{
\frac15,\frac14,\frac13,\frac25,\frac12,
\frac35,\frac23,\frac34,\frac45,1
\right\}.
$$

The true base atoms are a unit-$\ell_2$ Gaussian with width parameter $8$ and a unit-$\ell_2$ 30-sample linear ramp. Each atom is active exactly once in every frame, so

$$
\|X_{\mathrm{true}}\|_0=2T=160.
$$

## Flat initialization and ADMM settings

The reference dictionary initialization uses centered nonnegative flat atoms of widths 21 and 41 samples with zero coefficient initialization. The non-temporal prefit sets $\lambda_T=0$.

Both coefficient and dictionary blocks use over-relaxation

$$
\gamma_X=\gamma_D=1.8.
$$

Initial ADMM penalties are

$$
\rho_X^{(0)}=1000,\qquad \rho_D^{(0)}=500,
$$

with standard-residual adaptive updates every main iteration. For the coefficient block,

$$
r_X=\|X-Y\|_F,\qquad s_X=\rho_X\|Y-Y_{\mathrm{old}}\|_F,
$$

and for the dictionary block,

$$
r_D=\|D-G\|_F,\qquad s_D=\rho_D\|G-G_{\mathrm{old}}\|_F.
$$

A residual ratio threshold of 10 and multiplicative factor 2 are used, with inverse rescaling of the corresponding scaled dual variable whenever $\rho$ changes.

## Padded Fourier coefficient update

When $\lambda_T=0$, the reference implementation solves the quadratic coefficient subproblem directly in the padded Fourier domain. For one Fourier coordinate and frame,

$$
(\rho_XI+a^Ha)x=b,
$$

where

$$
b=a^HS_f+\rho_X\mathcal F(Y-U).
$$

The rank-one system is solved by Sherman--Morrison. The physical signal is pre-padded by $M-1$ zeros while each scaled dictionary filter is post-padded to

$$
L=N+M-1.
$$

The Python compatibility implementation reproduces this Fourier-domain algebra independently of the general coefficient solver.

# Alternating Gaussian/ramp recovery

## Diagnostic sparsity sweep

Because the selected MATLAB parameter files were unavailable, $\lambda_S$ was treated as unresolved and investigated diagnostically using known dictionary truth.

A coarse sweep gave:

| $\lambda_S$ | Clean error | Gaussian cosine | Ramp cosine | Significant coefficients |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.15 | 0.1384 | 0.9910 | 0.8702 | 287 |
| 0.20 | 0.1573 | 0.9903 | 0.8734 | 237 |
| 0.25 | 0.1990 | 0.9910 | 0.8818 | 179 |
| 0.30 | 0.2260 | 0.9842 | 0.8442 | 172 |
| 0.35 | 0.2974 | 0.9884 | 0.7192 | 203 |
| 0.40 | 0.3046 | 0.9793 | 0.6520 | 206 |

A refined sweep gave:

| $\lambda_S$ | Clean error | Gaussian cosine | Ramp cosine | Significant coefficients |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.22 | 0.1708 | 0.9905 | 0.8795 | 204 |
| 0.23 | 0.1796 | 0.9902 | 0.8817 | 195 |
| **0.24** | **0.1842** | **0.9904** | **0.8841** | **188** |
| 0.25 | 0.1990 | 0.9910 | 0.8818 | 179 |
| 0.26 | 0.2130 | 0.9910 | 0.8771 | 179 |
| 0.27 | 0.2272 | 0.9897 | 0.8748 | 178 |
| 0.28 | 0.2418 | 0.9879 | 0.8704 | 175 |

Ramp recovery has a smooth local maximum near $\lambda_S=0.24$. This value is retained only as the current 20 dB **oracle-development reference**. It is not an automatic or deployable parameter-selection result.

## 100-iteration flat-box prefit

For $\lambda_S=0.24$, the 100-iteration prefit produced

$$
\cos(g_{\mathrm{Gaussian}},d_{\mathrm{Gaussian}})=0.99035,
$$

and

$$
\cos(g_{\mathrm{ramp}},d_{\mathrm{ramp}})=0.88409.
$$

The clean reconstruction error was $0.18417$ and 188 coefficients exceeded $10^{-3}$.

The learned-versus-true cosine matrix was approximately

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
0.99035 & 0.77965\\
0.78754 & 0.88409
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

## Continued non-temporal MCDL

The learned dictionary and coefficients were used to initialize a second non-temporal MCDL stage. The sparse update remained in the logarithmic phase rather than restarting the initial 20-iteration $\ell_1$ warm-up.

After 200 additional main iterations,

$$
\cos(g_{\mathrm{Gaussian}},d_{\mathrm{Gaussian}})=0.99243,
$$

and

$$
\cos(g_{\mathrm{ramp}},d_{\mathrm{ramp}})=0.88441.
$$

The clean reconstruction error improved to

$$
0.16709,
$$

and the number of significant coefficients decreased to

$$
158,
$$

compared with 160 in truth.

The final similarity matrix was approximately

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
0.99243 & 0.78351\\
0.78415 & 0.88441
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Thus the second non-temporal stage improves reconstruction, Gaussian recovery, and sparse support recovery but does not materially sharpen the ramp beyond the prefit result. This is the current non-temporal learned-dictionary reference for evaluating temporal regularization.

# Current validation boundary

The following dictionary-learning components are now validated:

1. fixed-$X$, fixed-$\alpha$ dictionary forward operator;
2. dictionary adjoint and objective gradient;
3. SPD normal operator and matrix-free CG solve;
4. nonnegative finite-support unit-norm projection;
5. post-projection multiscale normalization;
6. noiseless known-$X$ one- and two-atom recovery;
7. MATLAB-compatible flat initialization;
8. reference Gaussian/ramp geometry and ten-scale grid;
9. reference L1-to-log sparse schedule;
10. adaptive coefficient and dictionary ADMM penalties;
11. padded Fourier-domain coefficient update;
12. controlled alternating coefficient/dictionary recovery on the 20 dB Gaussian/ramp problem.

Controlled joint coefficient/dictionary recovery is therefore validated for the reproduced 20 dB Gaussian/ramp benchmark. Validation of the complete temporally regularized learned-dictionary pipeline remains in progress.

# Next development milestone

The next phase is temporally regularized joint dictionary learning initialized from the validated Banco-style non-temporal prefit.

The planned progression is:

1. preserve the 20 dB Gaussian/ramp non-temporal result as a regression benchmark;
2. initialize the softmin temporal-regularized solve from the learned dictionary and coefficient representation;
3. determine an objective selection procedure for $\lambda_S$ and the temporal regularization parameter without using synthetic truth;
4. compare temporal and non-temporal learned dictionaries on identical noise realizations;
5. extend the validated workflow across SNR and independent noise realizations;
6. proceed to publication-scale Monte Carlo experiments only after the complete learned-dictionary pipeline is stable.

The current $\lambda_S=0.24$ is retained only as a 20 dB oracle-development reference.

# Discussion

The successful temporal coefficient model is geometric rather than pointwise. Barycentric motion supplies an efficient centerline prior; the spread term removes first-moment degeneracy; the squared gate permits finite-duration support; and full-state continuation addresses branch selection in the nonconvex solver.

The dictionary-learning work follows the same validation philosophy: identify linear operators and adjoints, validate them numerically, then introduce CG and alternating optimization only after those foundations are sound. Direct comparison with the reference MATLAB implementation established the flat initialization, rational scale geometry, sparse schedule, resampling conventions, Fourier coefficient update, and adaptive ADMM rules used in the Gaussian/ramp benchmark.

Parameter selection remains part of the estimator rather than an after-the-fact tuning step. The current $\lambda_S=0.24$ value was chosen with access to synthetic truth and is therefore useful only for development and oracle comparison. A deployable learned-dictionary estimator must select its regularization parameters using observable quantities such as discrepancy, tradeoff geometry, and stability.

# Conclusions

The proposed coefficient model combines logarithmic sparsity, barycentric trajectory motion, within-frame compactness, and smooth finite-duration gating. The formulation has explicit analytical gradients, avoids iterative transport subproblems, and supports reproducible automatic parameter selection.

The dictionary-learning extension is now validated beyond the fixed-coefficient setting. The reference 20 dB Gaussian/ramp experiment has been reproduced with MATLAB-compatible flat initialization, multiscale geometry, sparse scheduling, relaxation, adaptive ADMM penalties, and padded Fourier coefficient updates. With an oracle-development value of $\lambda_S=0.24$, the continued non-temporal MCDL solve recovers 158 significant coefficients versus 160 in truth, with Gaussian and ramp cosine similarities of approximately $0.9924$ and $0.8844$.

This stable non-temporal learned-dictionary result defines the baseline for the next phase: temporally regularized joint MCDL and objective regularization-parameter selection without access to synthetic truth.
